reply_text:
I've renumbered the requirements and sent the outline to a Codex seat to find which of them can have measurable outcomes. It's running now.

**The renumbering.** The requirements are now RQ-1 to RQ-9 (futon2 `a2caf1450`). None of them lines up with a row of the AIF model, and nothing else in futon2 or futon3c uses the RQ- prefix. The draft now says in a line that they aren't adaptations of R1–R19.

**What codex-proof2a is doing.** It's a read-only review. For each requirement it will give:
- **a metric:** which record, key path or git query, and the formula. It has to read a real record before naming a key.
- **today's value,** computed on today's records, with the command it used;
- **a threshold** and the window it applies over;
- **what new instrumentation is needed,** if any;
- **a verdict:** measurable now, measurable once instrumented, or not measurable as written. For the last, it must propose a rewording, a merge or a drop.

It will also check the plan's acceptance lines. I asked it to say plainly if "standing curiosity", "a generative model of itself" or "forward motion" make no observable difference.

It writes its findings to `futon2/holes/labs/wm-contract/NOTE-PROOF-2b-measurable-outcomes-2026-09-29.md`.
- Job: `invoke-1790711417111-27843-eca0fce2`
- I'm parked on it as `park-43440351-81d7-4c5c-bc2f-3ab681b86e1a`, with a one-hour deadline.

When it's back, I'll recompute one or two of its numbers and rewrite the requirements and acceptance lines in PROOF-2b with the measurable versions. I'll then tell you which ones got numbers and which were reworded or dropped.

The one-line data fix, step ⟨0⟩1, is still waiting for your OK. So are the three open questions at the end of PROOF-2b.

Codex's report checks out against the binding tally I made earlier: 5 abstained and 1 build-failed today. Now rewriting PROOF-2b's requirements and acceptance lines.Every requirement in PROOF-2b now has a number to check (futon2 `4690b26df`). Two were reworded because they didn't name anything observable: "a generative model of itself" (RQ-4) and "forward motion" (RQ-7). None was dropped. **Can I start with the new step ⟨0⟩0, a receipt at the end of every click, and the one-line data fix ⟨0⟩1?** Nothing in the plan can be checked until the receipt exists.

**What changed.** codex-proof2a's note (`NOTE-PROOF-2b-measurable-outcomes-2026-09-29.md`, `3631f87a0`) gave each requirement a metric on a named record, a threshold and today's value. I checked its tally of today's clicks (5 abstained, 1 build-failed) against my own count, and they match. Its main finding is that none of the nine can be measured from today's records. Seven become measurable once a specific field is recorded.

**The receipt is the first thing to build.** Five requirements (RQ-2, RQ-6, RQ-7, RQ-8, RQ-9) depend on one record. Each click ends in exactly one of:
- **an action receipt:** target, action kind, G terms, outcome, and the commit and reviewer if it changed anything;
- **a typed failure** with an id that the click loop's repair dispatch cites.

That's why it's now step ⟨0⟩0.

**The requirements now:**
- **Measurable once recorded:**
  - RQ-1: the field. Its check is exact set equality between what the decision considered and every unfinished Mission, Excursion, Ticket and algorithm at HEAD, not a matching count.
  - RQ-2: every click ends in an action or a failure sent to repair. Over a 20-click campaign that must hold for all 20, with at least one enacted action, so a campaign can't pass by failing 20 times.
  - RQ-3: curiosity. Every candidate records its information gain, and a paired control checks that an unread target scores better than an equally risky known one.
  - RQ-5: the model grows as well as shrinks. Two planted controls check that a new task file and an unexplained observation each add a state.
  - RQ-6: algorithm targets. One Tornhill run and one `write-algorithm` run per campaign, each with its commit and reviewer.
  - RQ-8: every action has a complete receipt.
  - RQ-9: every failure is typed and sent to repair within 5 minutes.
- **Reworded:**
  - **RQ-4** now requires a versioned list of model factors that covers the tasks, the stack's claims and the machine's own action and failure kinds. Every action has to show which factors it moved.
  - **RQ-7** is now counts per campaign, each tied to an action receipt: wants closed, tasks advanced, commits reviewed. At least one of those must be nonzero.
- **Today, every one of them is at zero** or not recorded. That's the baseline the first campaign will be compared against.

Your three open questions at the end of PROOF-2b are still open: which excursions go in the field, who approves a task's first interpretation, and whether gathering clicks count against the budget.
